name: Chicago
note: Configuration for chicago.html. The geography (lake shore, river, parks, streets, rail, buildings with heights) comes from OpenStreetMap via tools/fetch-osm.py and tools/build-chicago-osm.py into chicago-osm.json. This file holds what OSM does not: landmark decorations and cards, the detailed street corners, viewpoints. Positions are [lat, lon].

districts._: [name, hex colour, base height, tallest, box as [lat south, lon west, lat north, lon east]]; the first box that contains a block wins

landmarks.name: Willis Tower
landmarks.info: 233 S Wacker Dr · 1974 · 442 m, 108 floors, 527 m to the antenna tips. Nine bundled tubes stepping back at floors 50, 66 and 90.

landmarks.name: 875 North Michigan
landmarks.info: The John Hancock Center · 1969 · 344 m; 457 m to the antennas. A tapered tube with X-bracing on the outside.

landmarks.name: Trump International Hotel & Tower
landmarks.info: 401 N Wabash Ave · 2009 · 423 m with the spire. Its setbacks answer the heights of its neighbours along the river.

landmarks.name: Aon Center
landmarks.info: 200 E Randolph St · 1973 · 346 m. A plain white shaft, once clad in marble.

landmarks.name: St. Regis Chicago
landmarks.info: 363 E Wacker Dr · 2020 · 363 m. Three stems of stacked frusta (Jeanne Gang).

landmarks.name: Aqua
landmarks.info: 225 N Columbus Dr · 2009 · 262 m. Balconies of different depths make the facade ripple like water.

landmarks.name: Two Prudential Plaza
landmarks.info: 180 N Stetson Ave · 1990 · 303 m. Chevron setbacks and a spire.

landmarks.name: Marina City
landmarks.info: 300 N State St · 1964 · 179 m. Two 'corn cob' towers: spiral parking below, petal balconies above.

landmarks.name: Merchandise Mart
landmarks.info: 222 Merchandise Mart Plaza · 1930 · Four million square feet, once the largest building in the world.

landmarks.name: Chicago Board of Trade Building
landmarks.info: 141 W Jackson Blvd · 1930 · 184 m. Art Deco, closing the view down LaSalle Street; Ceres on top.

landmarks.name: 311 South Wacker Drive
landmarks.info: 311 S Wacker Dr · 1990 · 293 m. The glass crown is lit at night.

landmarks.name: Tribune Tower
landmarks.info: 435 N Michigan Ave · 1925 · 141 m. Neo-Gothic; stones from famous buildings are set into its base.

landmarks.name: Wrigley Building
landmarks.info: 400 N Michigan Ave · 1924 · 130 m. White terra cotta, floodlit at night.

landmarks.name: DuSable Bridge
landmarks.info: Michigan Avenue over the river · 1920 · a double-deck bascule bridge with four bridge houses carrying reliefs.

landmarks.name: Chicago Riverwalk
landmarks.info: The south bank of the Main Branch, a promenade of cafés, boat docks and the river theatre, from Lake Shore Drive to Lake Street.

landmarks.name: Water Tower Place
landmarks.info: 835 N Michigan Ave · 1976 · 262 m. A vertical mall under a hotel and apartments.

landmarks.name: Chicago Water Tower
landmarks.info: 806 N Michigan Ave · 1869 · 47 m. Limestone; one of the few buildings to survive the Great Fire of 1871.

landmarks.name: Fourth Presbyterian Church
landmarks.info: 126 E Chestnut St · 1914 · Gothic Revival, with a cloister garden on Michigan Avenue.

landmarks.name: The Drake Hotel
landmarks.info: 140 E Walton Pl · 1920 · the hotel at the top of the Magnificent Mile, facing Oak Street Beach.

landmarks.name: Crain Communications Building
landmarks.info: 150 N Michigan Ave · 1984 · 177 m. The slashed diamond top faces the park.

landmarks.name: Lake Point Tower
landmarks.info: 505 N Lake Shore Dr · 1968 · 197 m. Three curved wings; the only skyscraper east of Lake Shore Drive.

landmarks.name: Cloud Gate
landmarks.info: Millennium Park · 2006 · 'The Bean'. 168 stainless-steel plates, 20 m long; walk under its arch.

landmarks.name: Jay Pritzker Pavilion
landmarks.info: Millennium Park · 2004 · Frank Gehry. Stainless-steel ribbons over the stage, a trellis of pipes over the Great Lawn.

landmarks.name: Crown Fountain
landmarks.info: Millennium Park · 2004 · Jaume Plensa. Two glass-brick towers with the faces of Chicagoans, a black granite pool between.

landmarks.name: BP Pedestrian Bridge
landmarks.info: Millennium Park · 2004 · Frank Gehry's winding steel bridge over Columbus Drive to Maggie Daley Park.

landmarks.name: Buckingham Fountain
landmarks.info: Grant Park · 1927. One of the largest fountains in the world; the centre jet reaches 46 m.

landmarks.name: Art Institute of Chicago
landmarks.info: 111 S Michigan Ave · 1893. Beaux-Arts; the bronze lions guard the steps.

landmarks.name: Chicago Union Station
landmarks.info: 225 S Canal St · 1925. The Great Hall's skylight is 35 m up.

landmarks.name: Field Museum
landmarks.info: 1400 S Lake Shore Dr · 1921. Sue the T. rex lives inside.

landmarks.name: Shedd Aquarium
landmarks.info: 1200 S DuSable Lake Shore Dr · 1930. An octagonal Beaux-Arts hall on the lake.

landmarks.name: Adler Planetarium
landmarks.info: 1300 S DuSable Lake Shore Dr · 1930. America's first planetarium, at the end of the peninsula.

landmarks.name: Soldier Field
landmarks.info: 1410 Museum Campus Dr · 1924, rebuilt 2003. Home of the Bears; the colonnades survive.

landmarks.name: Navy Pier
landmarks.info: 600 E Grand Ave · 1916. A kilometre into the lake; the Centennial Wheel is 60 m tall.

landmarks.name: North Avenue Beach House
landmarks.info: 1603 N Lake Shore Dr · a beach house built like a steamship, with a rooftop deck.

landmarks.name: Lincoln Park Zoo
landmarks.info: 2001 N Clark St · 1868 · one of the oldest zoos in North America, and free.

landmarks.name: Wrigley Field
landmarks.info: 1060 W Addison St · 1914 · home of the Cubs. Ivy on the outfield walls, the hand-turned scoreboard in centre field, the red marquee at Clark and Addison.

landmarks.name: Montrose Harbor
landmarks.info: The northernmost harbour on this stretch of the lakefront, sheltered by Montrose Point.

landmarks.name: Montrose Beach
landmarks.info: Chicago's largest beach, north of the harbour, with dunes that are a protected habitat.

landmarks.name: Montrose Point Bird Sanctuary
landmarks.info: The Magic Hedge · a line of shrubs at the tip of Montrose Point where migrating birds land on the way across the lake.

landmarks.name: Lakefront Trail
landmarks.info: 18 miles of trail along the lake from Ardmore to 71st Street, split into bike and walking paths through most of this stretch.

landmarks.name: Belmont Harbor
landmarks.info: A harbour behind a long breakwater at the foot of Belmont Avenue.

landmarks.name: Diversey Harbor
landmarks.info: A lagoon harbour inside Lincoln Park, reached under Lake Shore Drive.

landmarks.name: Northwest Tower
landmarks.info: 1600 N Milwaukee Ave · 1929 · 12 storeys, Art Deco at the six corners; now The Robey hotel.

landmarks.name: Flat Iron Building
landmarks.info: 1579 N Milwaukee Ave · 1913 · a three-storey wedge where Milwaukee Avenue meets North Avenue.

landmarks.name: Wicker Park Fountain
landmarks.info: Wicker Park · a 2002 recreation of the park's original cast-iron fountain.

landmarks.name: Pulaski Park Fieldhouse
landmarks.info: 1419 W Blackhawk St · 1914 · William Carbys Zimmermann; gymnasium, auditorium and theatre.

landmarks.name: St. Stanislaus Kostka Church
landmarks.info: 1351 W Evergreen Ave · 1881 · Chicago's first Polish parish.

landmarks.name: Holy Trinity Polish Mission (Holy Trinity Catholic Church)
landmarks.info: 1118 N Noble St · 1906 · a Polish Baroque basilica with twin towers.

landmarks.name: St. Mary of the Angels
landmarks.info: 1850 N Hermitage Ave · 1920 · a copper dome modelled on St Peter's, over Bucktown.

el._: the L's elevated structure and trains follow the OSM tracks tagged as bridges

focus.name: Magnificent Mile
focus._: Michigan Avenue from the river to Oak Street: planters, street lights, signals, shoppers; no parking
